knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)

# What this does

Fits one DESeq2 model per contrast defined by script 02 and saves the fitted object, so the
shrinkage step (script 04) runs on its own instead of needing an interactive session. For each
contrast, exactly as the original analysis did:

1. subset the clean count matrix to the contrast's samples, leaving out the mitochondrial
   loci listed by script 01 (the mitogenome genes and their nuclear copies, analysed on their
   own in script 13), so the genome results and the GO enrichment built on them carry one
   nuclear gene per row;
2. set the design variable's levels explicitly (reference first) and fit `~ <variable>`;
3. check that the second coefficient is `<variable>_<test>_vs_<reference>`, which fixes the
   sign of every log2 fold change;
4. keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least a third of the contrast's samples (applied
   after fitting, as before).

Writes `03_analyses/dds/<contrast>.rds` (the filtered `DESeqDataSet`; git-ignored, rebuilt by
this script) and `03_analyses/DEG_lists/filter_summary.csv`. The PCA plots this script drew until
2026-10-17 are now step 14's (every sample set, with and without the lab control).

```{r paths}
source(here::here("01_code", "_paths.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DESeq2))
gcm <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(cnt, "gene_count_matrix_clean.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
mtl <- read.csv(file.path(cnt, "mitochondrial_loci.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(mtl$gene %in% rownames(gcm)))
gcm <- gcm[!rownames(gcm) %in% mtl$gene, ]                 # nuclear genes only (see step 1 above)
cat("mitochondrial rows left out:", nrow(mtl), "| genes kept:", nrow(gcm), "\n")
ti  <- read.csv(file.path(cnt, "treatmentinfo_clean.csv"), row.names = 1, colClasses = "character")
contrasts <- read.csv(file.path(deg, "contrasts.csv"), colClasses = "character")
cs        <- read.csv(file.path(deg, "contrast_samples.csv"), colClasses = "character")
stopifnot(all(cs$sample.1 %in% colnames(gcm)))
```

# Fit each contrast

```{r fit}
fit_one <- function(row) {
  smp <- cs$sample.1[cs$code == row$code]
  cd  <- ti[smp, c("tissue", "treatment", "day")]
  cd[[row$design_var]] <- factor(cd[[row$design_var]], levels = c(row$ref_level, row$test_level))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(cd[[row$design_var]]))
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(gcm[, smp], cd, reformulate(row$design_var))
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
  coef_name <- sprintf("%s_%s_vs_%s", row$design_var, row$test_level, row$ref_level)
  stopifnot(resultsNames(dds)[2] == coef_name)
  keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= ncol(dds) / 3
  saveRDS(dds[keep, ], file.path(dds_dir, paste0(row$code, ".rds")))
  data.frame(code = row$code, family = row$family, coefficient = coef_name,
             n_samples = ncol(dds), genes_in_matrix = nrow(dds), genes_after_filter = sum(keep))
}
summary_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(contrasts)), function(i) fit_one(contrasts[i, ])))
write.csv(summary_tbl, file.path(deg, "filter_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary_tbl)
```
